title: Release candidate 2 on paper, batch 2: pages 4 to 9, About this release candidate, the part opener and chapter 1
how: Six photographs of pages 4 to 9 of the printed candidate, sent out of page order and put back in order here; the notes continue the numbering of batch 1 from 14. The handwriting was read by the journalist; four readings were uncertain, and Dinis confirmed them the same day (notes 31, 36, 49, 51).

first-page.name: The first pages sell the book
first-page.principle: Every step of attention buys the next (Zoom in, not discover).

show.name: Show the book, do not list it
show.principle: The opening is a best of; the first page shows the art of the possible (Zoom in, not discover).

altitude.name: Topics first, details under them
altitude.principle: The book zooms in: detail comes after the point, never before it (Zoom in, not discover).

process-out.name: The making-of out of the reader's way
process-out.principle: How the book was made, and the 2018 book, go to a section at the end (the first batch, sign-off 5).

voice.name: The voice is mine
voice.principle: The book is in Dinis's voice; a line that sounds harsh, odd or not like him is rewritten, and family stays out.

reader-context.name: Meet the reader where they are
reader-context.principle: Say what a term means before using it, link the source, and tell the reader how to read the book.

release.name: A release, not a draft
release.principle: The release candidate is shipped and sold; it should read as a book, not as a working document.

notes.written: the ZX FOUNDER doesn't care yet → maybe at the end of the Book
notes.means: The reader does not care how the book was made, not yet: About this release candidate moves to the end.

notes.written: is this a better name than ZX developer?
notes.means: A naming question: is 'ZX founder' a better name for the reader than 'ZX developer'? (Asked again on page 8.)

notes.written: logistics
notes.means: How the chapters say where their sources ran out is logistics, not reading.

notes.written: this is the story & workflow detail ↓ then they should not be here
notes.means: The story of rc1 and the workflow do not belong on page 4.

notes.written: remove
notes.means: Remove the paragraph about placeholder chapters from the reader's book.

notes.written: WRONG [over: not a version]
notes.means: 'This is a candidate, not a version' is wrong: this is a release.

notes.written: this is an RC which will be added to Leanpub & sold ✓ ... i.e. we are selling & shipping this book now
notes.means: The release candidate goes on Leanpub and is sold, now.

notes.written: this RCx → RELEASE CANDIDATE ↓ i.e. this should be a release → not a draft
notes.means: Spell out 'release candidate', and treat it as a release, not a draft.

pages.name: Page 5, the end of About this release candidate

notes.written: Not to me [over: Then, if you are Dinis,] ... I am :) [over: read it with a pen]
notes.means: The book should not talk to Dinis; it talks to the reader. (And yes, he is reading it with a pen.)

notes.written: we need to tell the reader that if they are reading this on a screen they should stop ↓ and print this book
notes.means: Tell the reader to print it: the book is meant to be read on paper.

notes.written: here we should have a section pointing to the website of this book & · show what is there, namely the tools & visualisations · show where to find the chapter PDFs (for print)
notes.means: A section that points to the book's website: what is there, the tools and visualisations, and the chapter PDFs for print.

notes.written: VERY important → explain that this entire book content is released under CC-BY which means they are free to · copy it · distribute it · sell it · remix. All they need to do is to have a small credit of where the text came from ... CC-BY is a copyright licence that gives the reader rights
notes.means: Explain CC BY in plain words: copy, distribute, sell, remix, with a small credit.

notes.written: page 5 and "why am I reading this book?" + "why should I continue"
notes.means: By page 5 the reader still does not know why to read the book, or why to go on.

notes.written: infographic and/or graph visualization of this part
notes.means: Every part opener gets a picture of the part: an infographic or a graph.

notes.written: too harsh voice [under: what I want]
notes.means: 'What I want to have happened' sounds harsh; rewrite in a warmer voice.

notes.written: you finish chapter one, part one and the book [under: by the time you close the book]
notes.means: Say what the reader will have by the end of chapter 1, of part 1 and of the book: milestones, not one finish line.

notes.written: Don't mention my daughters ↓ say "kids" or "children"
notes.means: No daughters in the book: say kids or children.

notes.written: now [circled: are not]
notes.means: Wrong as written: a lot of Generation Z are now looking for a job, not 'not looking'. (Dinis confirmed the reading.)

notes.written: find better word [struck: hungry]
notes.means: 'Hungry' is the wrong word for Generation Z; find a better one.

notes.written: to harsh [under: what I want]
notes.means: The same 'what I want' again: too harsh.

notes.written: (1) → link to article ← here or at the end of this section or book
notes.means: The Expert founders needs a link to the article: in place, or at the end of the section or the book.

notes.written: they didn't, agents are a 2026 thing [circled: one grew up with the agents]
notes.means: Wrong: Generation Z did not grow up with agents; agents are a 2026 thing.

notes.written: wrong story, since either could have built it
notes.means: The story goes both ways: Generation X can build it and impress Generation Z, or build a game or an app for them; not only the young one building what the older one described. (Dinis confirmed the reading.)

notes.written: this kind of detail is not needed [and struck: Boundaries differ between sources ... I still mean it.]
notes.means: The Pew dates paragraph is detail the opening does not need.

notes.written: weird, not me [over: and now cannot give up]
notes.means: 'And now cannot give up' does not sound like Dinis.

notes.written: show storyboard here :)
notes.means: Put the storyboard panel with the ZX Spectrum here, in the chapter.

notes.written: NR → Not Relevant [over the XZ paragraph, struck with a wave]
notes.means: The XZ paragraph is not relevant: cut it.

notes.written: REF [over: explorer coding]
notes.means: Explorer coding needs a reference.

notes.written: readers don't know about Wardley maps or what I mean by "explorer"
notes.means: Explain explorer (and Wardley maps) before using the word.

notes.written: ZX FOUNDER? :) [after: You can be the founder.]
notes.means: The name again: 'ZX founder', next to 'You can be the founder'.

notes.written: this is at the end [beside: limited company in the UK, the case for Lithuania, Portugal]
notes.means: The list of countries belongs at the end, with the company chapters.

notes.written: move to end [beside: Two honest clauses about that list]
notes.means: The two honest clauses move to the end.

notes.written: I don't think we should talk or mention too much what was on the other book → this is going to be a big rewrite ↳ maybe on that section at the end about how this book was written and evolved
notes.means: Less of the 2018 book: this is a big rewrite, and the 2018 story goes to the section at the end on how the book was written and evolved.

notes.written: Finally we tell the reader why they should read this book :)
notes.means: This paragraph, the shape of the middle and 'Ship', is the reason to read the book; it arrives on page 9.

notes.written: too much detail at this stage of the book
notes.means: Build it without a server, SG/Send, sgit and RiskMandate are too much detail for chapter 1.

notes.written: yes, point to our website (of this book) where ALL materials are public → first version of this site will have my own startups :)
notes.means: The measure: point to the book's website, where all the materials are public; its first version will list Dinis's own startups as the first examples. (Dinis confirmed 'startups'.)

notes.written: new book [circled: new book that]
notes.means: The answer to 'second edition or a new book?': a new book.

notes.written: But I really like this kind of box, but it means we need two [PDFs, two views]
notes.means: Keep the boxes, in a second edition of each release candidate: the release edition, ready to sell with nothing draft in it, and a reviewer edition, for any reviewer, with notes, questions and places to answer. (Dinis confirmed and explained; decision 018.)

chapter_one.what: Chapter 1 of rc2, paragraph by paragraph, with what the notes ask for each, for the cut map drawing.

blocks.first: The first line of the 2018 book was this
This edition needs a longer first line
In 2018 I wrote that Generation Z was
The second reader is my own generation
In The expert founders I put the change
Often the two readers are in the same family
The dates I use are the Pew Research Center's
One more thing about the name (XZ)
The 2018 book had a chapter called Be a founder
So this book has an objective
Two honest clauses about that list
The shape of the middle follows from the objective
Then Build it without a server
A book that is a book to read is fine
That means asking you to tell us
For Dinis: the measure; second edition or new book
